It was a loss, not just to the Lot'dy, but the Naga as well. Without their squires, the Naga would have to risk themselves. A leviathan Lord was too valuable to risk, if the rider died, they would lose the beast. Which is why the squires fought first. It would take time to train more, not everyone could tolerate the poison.

Tasting the knife, killed most would be squires. The ceremony involved knives, and poison, from the Leviathans. Even now the thought of it made Sa'vak feel sick. He had shaken for days after, but he had lived. Even then, Leviathans killed most of those who survived. In fairness, the beasts killed most Naga who tried to bond them. They were even worse with the Ha'lot'dy. So it was, that even amongst the Naga, Sa'vak was high ranking, speaking with the authority of Saoirse. Among the Ha'lot'dy, he was a legend.

Serenity was as different as the Naga who lived there. The great pressure drew water out of the cave systems. Behind the great cliffs, was a second city, a city without water. The Naga had originally used the caves, to begin breathing. As they had developed the ability, they had begun making a more permanent residence. It had grown into an entire city. Most Naga couldn't sleep there, but the Ha'lot'dy did. It was the base of the Legion. It housed the Temples of Zille and Umbralocht. It was the centre of Serenity. [The Sanctum](http://ultraimg.com/images/image94388.jpg), the inner city, and the place Sa'vak loved most.

He was home, but he couldn't sleep. He kept going over the engagement at the beach. If he had been faster, his friends would be alive. He knew it was dangerous to dwell on the past. Sometimes, you just had to get it out of your system, so Sa'vak drank. He sat quietly in the legions hall, on the table in front of him, sat his amulet. The symbol of Umbralocht. They were weak, the dead. Umbralocht doesn't protect the weak. He knew this to be true, the weak failed. He still felt like shit. He should have been better.

A silence came over the hall. Every legionnaire stood. There at the entrance, stood royalty. Saoirse. She motioned for him to stay seated, honouring him among the legion, he stood anyway. She snaked her way over to his table, and sat, if a Naga could be said to sit. The hall held its breath, Naga did not come here. She motioned for him to sit again, this time he obeyed. "The goddess calls Sa'vak, are you ready", she asked? "Yes, always" he said. "Aluth has grown, we had to open his pen", Saoirse said. "How" asked Sa'vak, "that's impossible"?"It would seem not, get your things Sa'vak, we are leaving", with that she stood, and Sa'vak's short stay was over.

Linux noob here, what exact is KDE?

KDE is short for K-Tolls Desktop Environment. It's the system behind your graphic user interface (GUI).

The easiest way I've found to explain this is to visualize different versions of Windows: Think of WinXP and Win7.

In WinXP you had a blue taskbar and a green, elongated START button with a Windows logo and the word "START". In Win7 you have a blue, round START button with only a Windows logo, and the taskbar color can be changed and it incorporates a transparency.

Also, between the two, icons are different. Some of the applications are different, as XP had MSDos and Win7 came with Command Prompt and Powershell. Animations are almost nonexistent in XP and Win7 has animations when you maximize/minimize windows, open programs, and open menus.

Essentially, the way these two similar-but-different operating systems looks and behaves is different... even though the underlying code and functionality is exactly the same.

This is how different DE's behave. You have the same underlying Linux code below, so the functionality and structure is exactly the same. But different DE's have different looks, animations, and packages.

KDE tends to have a myriad of transitions, animations, transparencies, and other elaborate resource-hog items which I call flair. This flair is non-essential add-ons which make the DE "prettier," but not more functional. So, for this reason, I usually don't use KDE, and I don't recommend anyone use it on older hardware.
So basically KDE is just "prettier"? Also sounds like KDE isn't gear towards the more economy tiered laptops.

Pretty much...

KDE is also is also built on K-tools, which is now referred to as Qt... which is a coding toolkit. If you're using Mint now, your apps are probably GTK, which probably doesn't mean much to you now... but some people are diehard Qt or GTK fanboys. Honestly, they're about the same to me.

But, yes. KDE is prettier and smoother. It also has a couple of packages which are specific to itself, as with any DE. What I mean by that is that it uses its own Konqueror file browser, Konsole terminal emulator, Kalgebra calculator, and others. These are standard packages, but they have specific features and options designed for KDE... as you'll find when comparing any two different DE's.

Its a "desktop environment" (DE). Its the GUI that sits on top of your terminal and gives you windows, a taskbar, a mouse, etc.

So, Linux is a kernel, its the foundation. Linux Mint is a distribution, it collects all the extra software and packages it up for you. Cinnamon is the normal DE, which is like the carpet, the doors, and the paint on the walls. It shows you the stuff you have. Linux mint comes with Cinnamon by default, but Mate and KDE are alternative options.
